title: WSI-Babel-Shark: A modular pipeline for robust metadata extraction from heterogeneous whole slide image labels in digital pathology

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《WSI-Babel-Shark: A modular pipeline for robust metadata extraction from heterogeneous whole slide image labels in digital pathology》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction and objectives · p0075】Reliable slide-level metadata are essential for modern digital pathology workflows. They enable the linkage of whole-slide images (WSIs) with corresponding cases in lab information systems (LIS) and picture archiving and communication systems (PACS). Accurate metadata ensure traceability, facilitate automated data integration, and support downstream analyses as well as FAIR data stewardship.1, 2 In routine diagnostic practice, barcode-based identifiers typically provide this linkage by encoding case and block information directly on slide labels, allowing scanners and LIS interfaces to synchronize records automatically.3 However, when barcode identifiers are missing, unreadable, or inconsistent across systems, automated linkage becomes non-trivial and requires robust text-based extraction from label images.

【Introduction and objectives · p0080】In research, archival, and biobank settings, barcode-based identifiers are often missing, damaged, or do not align with institutional standards. The problem is further compounded by the high variability of label designs across scanners and institutions. Differences in typography, label orientation, and the presence of handwritten elements pose major challenges for optical character recognition (OCR)-based metadata extraction.4 Several open-source frameworks provide essential infrastructure for digital pathology, such as OpenSlide for vendor-neutral WSI access5 and DICOM-based standards for metadata representation.6, 7 Yet, only a few recent approaches have addressed the practical challenge of automatically extracting structured metadata from heterogeneous label layouts. Whereas some OCR-based methods, such as AutoLDP,8 have demonstrated high accuracy for standardized label formats, most existing tools still rely on fixed spatial and semantic rules or manually defined regions of interest (ROIs), which limits their scalability and adaptability in multi-institutional settings.4, 8 Consequently, there remains a need for a metadata extraction framework that can automatically adapt to heterogeneous label layouts, detect previously unseen label structures, recover metadata when barcode information is incomplete or unavailable, and be designed for deployment across different scanner platforms and institutional workflows.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《WSI-Babel-Shark: A modular pipeline for robust metadata extraction from heterogeneous whole slide image labels in digital pathology》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Evaluation design · p0355】The evaluation strategy of WSI-Babel-Shark was designed to comprehensively assess both the performance of the label-layout classifier and the robustness of the complete metadata extraction pipeline under realistic diagnostic conditions. All experiments were performed on datasets that were entirely independent of those used for classifier training and development, ensuring unbiased and reproducible results.

【Materials and methods · p0100】This section outlines the datasets, architecture, and evaluation procedures used to develop and validate the WSI-Babel-Shark framework. We first describe the characteristics and sources of the datasets, followed by details of the modular pipeline architecture, including data matrix code decoding, layout classification, ROI-based OCR, and rule-based parsing. Subsequent subsections explain the classifier design, graphical annotation tools, and evaluation strategy used to assess performance, robustness, and reproducibility. The section concludes with implementation details and information on code and data availability.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《WSI-Babel-Shark: A modular pipeline for robust metadata extraction from heterogeneous whole slide image labels in digital pathology》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Classifier performance · p0475】The label-layout classifier showed strong performance in assigning slides to the correct layout group. On the closed-set test set, which included 20% of the 1836 manually annotated samples, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 97.41%. Class-wise precision, recall, and F1-scores are summarized in Table 1, demonstrating consistently high performance across the 10 predefined layout groups, with macro-averaged precision and recall values of 0.98 and 0.97, respectively.

【Pipeline performance · p0510】Field-level analysis demonstrated high extraction accuracy across the individual metadata components. The case number and year were correctly extracted for all 267 evaluable slides. Three extraction errors were observed for the lab identifier, three for the pot identifier, three for the block identifier, and three for the stain annotation. Because multiple metadata fields were incorrect in some slides, these errors were distributed across nine slides rather than representing independent failure cases. The observed extraction errors were associated with degraded label quality, including low print contrast, partial label damage, glare artifacts, handwritten markings, mixed-format stain annotations, and OCR confusion between visually similar individual characters or digits during character-level recognition.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《WSI-Babel-Shark: A modular pipeline for robust metadata extraction from heterogeneous whole slide image labels in digital pathology》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Fig. 1 · f0005】Fig. 1 Distribution of sample counts across groups (G1–G10).The figure illustrates the number of slides in each group, ranging from 27 samples in G10 to 398 samples in G1.

【Fig. 2 · f0010】Fig. 2 Representative examples of the 10 manually defined label-layout groups (G1–G10) used in WSI-Babel-Shark.Each panel illustrates the characteristic spatial arrangement of metadata fields used for ROI definition and subsequent metadata extraction. Colored text denotes the metadata fields extracted by the pipeline: Lab ID (red), Case number (blue), Year/Date (green), Staining (dark red), Block number (orange), Pot identifier (olive), and Section number (teal). All remaining text shown in black represents layout-specific information, including manufacturer labels, lab abbreviations, lot numbers, auxiliary numeric codes, and other institution-specific printed elements that are not used for SlideID generation. When an alphanumeric code is present (e.g., A1), the alphabetic character represents the Pot identifier, whereas the following numeric character represents the Block number. Stand-alone numeric values appearing separately on the label correspond to the Section number. (For interpretation of the references to color in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)

【Fig. 3 · f0015】Fig. 3 Workflow of the WSI-Babel-Shark main pipeline.The flowchart illustrates the sequential execution of all processing modules coordinated by runner.py under centralized YAML configuration control. The unified command-line interface implemented in cli_main.py manages ROI-based metadata extraction and fallback operations. Together, these modules enable fully automated and reproducible processing of whole-slide images—from initial slide collection and label extraction to data matrix code decoding, stain identification, SlideID generation, and integration of all metadata into the structured SQLite registry.
